title: A Basket of New Fruit Varieties
title_full: A basket of new fruit varieties is coming your way
subtitle: Gene Editing & the Future of Fruit — Reading Courseware
source: By The Economist, adapted by Newsela staff on 05.11.26
article_lead: Humans have bred crops for desirable traits for many thousands of years. Now, they are looking to gene editing as a way of creating new fruit varieties.
article_full:
Opening
Humans have bred crops for desirable traits for many thousands of years. Now, they are looking to gene editing as a way of creating new fruit varieties. "You don't notice the seeds in a blackberry until you've tried a seedless one," says Tom Adams. He is the head of Pairwise. It is a company in North Carolina. It is working on the first blackberries that don't have seeds. Pairwise is using gene editing to make its seedless blackberries. Gene editing is a method that lets scientists change the DNA of plants. Genes are pieces of DNA. They contain the instructions for building a living thing. Editing genes can change how a living thing looks. For example, it can change how seeds develop. Technically, these blackberries still have seeds. They are just so small and soft that you don't notice them.

Changing Fruits
Fruits have changed a lot. About 12,000 years ago, humans stopped being hunter-gatherers. They stopped traveling to find food. Instead they started to grow their own food. Over thousands of years, humans have grown fruit to their tastes. They picked the plants that bore the tastiest fruits or vegetables and bred them to create new plants. This is called selective breeding. It is also known as artificial selection. This is in contrast to natural selection. In nature, living things that are best suited to their environment survive and have more offspring. These are not always the ones with the tastiest fruits. But thousands of years of selective breeding have led to tastier, hardier, and often larger fruits and vegetables. Today's peaches are much larger than their wild ancestors, for example. Selectively bred fruits also tend to be sweeter.

Changing Fruits
Now gene editing allows scientists to make changes to plants even more quickly and precisely. CRISPR is the most popular such technique at the moment. It is a technology that allows scientists to change the DNA of an organism. It can change or remove specific genes. That would be hard to do through selective breeding. Computer software like artificial intelligence (AI) is also helping scientists design fruit. With AI, computers and machines can learn and solve problems using information. Using AI, scientists are able to discover more about certain traits, such as the chemicals that generate flavor.

Slowing Reactions
Chemical reactions are when substances change into new substances. Scientists are looking to slow chemical reactions in other fruits and veggies to make them look more appealing and even last longer. For example, avocados (yes, they are a fruit!) turn brown when you cut into them. That's because an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase reacts with the oxygen in the air in a process that causes browning. Enzymes can speed up chemical reactions and are also responsible for the ripening process, which means enzymes can change the texture, color, and flavor of food, too. GreenVenus, a Californian firm, is using CRISPR to develop avocados that don't turn brown. They changed how the enzyme is made in the fruit. Scientists have also developed mushrooms and potatoes that inhibit the same enzyme. So, slowing that reaction down makes mushrooms and potatoes last longer, and they don't turn brown as fast.

Ready To Eat?
So far, a few fruits that have been gene-edited with CRISPR have gone on sale. That's because it takes a long time to grow most fruit. It can take several years for apple or peach trees to begin bearing fruit. But as more fruity creations go on sale, companies believe that more people will eat fruit. Pairwise estimates that their seedless blackberries could become as popular as easy-peel mandarins.

patterns.definition_en: Reports what someone or an organization predicts or calculates.

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A type or kind of something; a particular form of a plant or animal.

grade10.sentence: This new variety of rice can grow well in dry areas.
grade10.translation: 这种水稻新品种能在干旱地区良好生长。

all_vocab_items.other_usage: a wide variety of 各种各样的

all_vocab_items.definition_en: To keep animals or plants in order to produce young or new plants with particular qualities.

article_example.sentence: They picked the plants that bore the tastiest fruits or vegetables and bred them to create new plants.
article_example.translation: 他们挑选结出最美味水果或蔬菜的植物，并培育它们以创造新植物。

zhongkao.sentence: Farmers breed chickens for fresh eggs.
zhongkao.translation: 农民饲养鸡以获取新鲜鸡蛋。

grade10.sentence: Scientists breed new types of wheat to resist disease.
grade10.translation: 科学家培育新型小麦以抵抗疾病。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Worth having or wanting; attractive or useful.

article_example.sentence: Humans have bred crops for desirable traits for many thousands of years.
article_example.translation: 人类几千年来一直在培育具有理想性状的作物。

zhongkao.sentence: Good communication skills are desirable for this job.
zhongkao.translation: 良好的沟通能力是这份工作的理想条件。

grade10.sentence: Living in a quiet neighborhood is highly desirable for families.
grade10.translation: 对于家庭来说，住在安静的社区是非常理想的。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A part of a cell that controls the development and appearance of a living thing.

article_example.sentence: Genes are pieces of DNA. They contain the instructions for building a living thing.
article_example.translation: 基因是DNA的片段。它们包含构建生命体的指令。

zhongkao.sentence: Eye color is decided partly by your genes.
zhongkao.translation: 眼睛颜色部分由基因决定。

grade10.sentence: Scientists study genes to understand how diseases develop.
grade10.translation: 科学家研究基因以了解疾病如何发展。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Detailed information on how to do something; a command or direction.

article_example.sentence: They contain the instructions for building a living thing.
article_example.translation: 它们包含构建生命体的指令。

zhongkao.sentence: Please read the instructions before using the machine.
zhongkao.translation: 使用机器前请阅读说明。

grade10.sentence: The teacher gave clear instructions on how to write the essay.
grade10.translation: 老师清楚地说明了如何写这篇作文。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: To grow or cause to grow and become more advanced; to create something new.

article_example.sentence: For example, it can change how seeds develop.
article_example.translation: 例如，它可以改变种子发育的方式。

zhongkao.sentence: Children develop quickly in their first five years.
zhongkao.translation: 儿童在最初五年里发展很快。

grade10.sentence: The company is developing a new app for language learning.
grade10.translation: 该公司正在开发一款语言学习新应用。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Carefully choosing only the best or most suitable.

article_example.sentence: This is called selective breeding.
article_example.translation: 这被称为选择性育种。

zhongkao.sentence: She is very selective about the books she reads.
zhongkao.translation: 她对读什么书非常挑剔。

grade10.sentence: Selective schools choose students based on test results.
grade10.translation: 择优录取的学校根据考试成绩选拔学生。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: The process of producing plants or animals with particular qualities.

article_example.sentence: But thousands of years of selective breeding have led to tastier, hardier, and often larger fruits and vegetables.
article_example.translation: 但数千年的选择性育种使水果和蔬菜变得更美味、更耐寒，且往往更大。

zhongkao.sentence: Dog breeding requires patience and knowledge.
zhongkao.translation: 狗的培育需要耐心和知识。

grade10.sentence: Plant breeding programs aim to improve crop yields.
grade10.translation: 植物育种项目旨在提高作物产量。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Made by people; not natural.

article_example.sentence: It is also known as artificial selection.
article_example.translation: 它也被称为人工选择。

zhongkao.sentence: This lake is artificial, not natural.
zhongkao.translation: 这个湖是人造的，不是天然的。

grade10.sentence: Artificial intelligence is changing many industries.
grade10.translation: 人工智能正在改变许多行业。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A person or animal from whom others have descended; an early form of something.

article_example.sentence: Today's peaches are much larger than their wild ancestors, for example.
article_example.translation: 例如，今天的桃子比它们的野生祖先大得多。

zhongkao.sentence: My ancestors came from a small village in the south.
zhongkao.translation: 我的祖先来自南方的一个小村庄。

grade10.translation: 科学家将现代鸟类与其恐龙祖先进行比较。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Exactly; in a way that is accurate and exact.

article_example.sentence: Now gene editing allows scientists to make changes to plants even more quickly and precisely.
article_example.translation: 现在，基因编辑使科学家能够更快、更精确地改变植物。

zhongkao.sentence: Please tell me precisely what happened.
zhongkao.translation: 请准确告诉我发生了什么。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A living thing, especially one that is very small or simple.

article_example.translation: 这是一项使科学家能够改变生物体DNA的技术。

zhongkao.sentence: A microscope helps us see tiny organisms in water.
zhongkao.translation: 显微镜帮助我们看到水中的微小生物。

grade10.sentence: Every organism depends on its environment to survive.
grade10.translation: 每个生物体都依赖环境来生存。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A particular quality in someone's character or in a plant or animal.

article_example.translation: 利用AI，科学家能够发现更多关于某些性状的信息，例如产生风味的化学物质。

zhongkao.sentence: Honesty is an important character trait.

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A particular type of solid, liquid, or gas.

article_example.translation: 化学反应是物质变成新物质的过程。

zhongkao.sentence: Water is the most common substance on Earth.
zhongkao.translation: 水是地球上最常见的物质。

grade10.sentence: The lab handles dangerous chemical substances with great care.
grade10.translation: 实验室非常小心地处理危险的化学物质。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: A substance produced by a living organism that helps a chemical reaction happen.

article_example.sentence: That's because an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase reacts with the oxygen in the air in a process that causes browning.
article_example.translation: 那是因为一种叫做多酚氧化酶的酶与空气中的氧气发生反应，导致褐变。

zhongkao.translation: 我们胃里的酶帮助消化食物。

grade10.translation: 科学家改变了水果中酶的生成方式。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Attractive or interesting; pleasing.

article_example.sentence: Scientists are looking to slow chemical reactions in other fruits and veggies to make them look more appealing and even last longer.

zhongkao.sentence: The colorful poster looks very appealing to children.

all_vocab_items.definition_en: To guess or calculate the cost, size, or value of something.

all_vocab_items.definition_en: The young of an animal or plant; children or descendants.

article_example.translation: 在自然界中，最适应环境的生物会存活下来并产生更多后代。

zhongkao.translation: 猫和它的后代住在我们的花园里。

grade10.sentence: Survival of the fittest means those best adapted produce more offspring.

all_vocab_items.definition_en: To slow down or prevent a process or reaction.

article_example.translation: 科学家还开发了能抑制同一种酶的蘑菇和土豆。

all_vocab_items.definition_en: Choosing plants or animals with desired qualities to produce the next generation.

article_example.translation: 但数千年的选择性育种使水果和蔬菜变得更美味、更耐寒，且往往更大。

paragraphs.title: Opening
sentences: Humans have bred crops for desirable traits for many thousands of years.
Now, they are looking to gene editing as a way of creating new fruit varieties.
"You don't notice the seeds in a blackberry until you've tried a seedless one," says Tom Adams.
He is the head of Pairwise.
It is a company in North Carolina.
It is working on the first blackberries that don't have seeds.
Pairwise is using gene editing to make its seedless blackberries.
Gene editing is a method that lets scientists change the DNA of plants.
Genes are pieces of DNA.
They contain the instructions for building a living thing.
Editing genes can change how a living thing looks.
For example, it can change how seeds develop.
Technically, these blackberries still have seeds.
They are just so small and soft that you don't notice them.

socratic.q: Why might consumers prefer seedless blackberries over regular ones?
socratic.a: Because seeds can be annoying to bite into; seedless blackberries offer a smoother eating experience, which makes them more appealing to consumers.

socratic.q: What role do genes play in how a living thing looks or develops?
socratic.a: Genes contain instructions for building a living thing, so editing genes can change appearance and development, such as how seeds form.

socratic.q: Does 'seedless' in this article mean there are absolutely no seeds? Explain.
socratic.a: No. The text says the blackberries technically still have seeds, but they are so small and soft that you don't notice them.

paragraphs.title: Changing Fruits (History)
sentences: Fruits have changed a lot.
About 12,000 years ago, humans stopped being hunter-gatherers.
They stopped traveling to find food.
Instead they started to grow their own food.
Over thousands of years, humans have grown fruit to their tastes.
They picked the plants that bore the tastiest fruits or vegetables and bred them to create new plants.
This is called selective breeding.
It is also known as artificial selection.
This is in contrast to natural selection.
In nature, living things that are best suited to their environment survive and have more offspring.
These are not always the ones with the tastiest fruits.
But thousands of years of selective breeding have led to tastier, hardier, and often larger fruits and vegetables.
Today's peaches are much larger than their wild ancestors, for example.
Selectively bred fruits also tend to be sweeter.

socratic.q: What major change in human lifestyle happened about 12,000 years ago?
socratic.a: Humans stopped being hunter-gatherers and began growing their own food instead of traveling to find it.

socratic.q: How is artificial selection different from natural selection when it comes to fruit taste?
socratic.a: In artificial selection, humans choose plants with the tastiest fruits to breed; in natural selection, survival depends on fitness to the environment, not taste.

socratic.q: What evidence shows that selective breeding has changed fruits over time?
socratic.a: Today's peaches are much larger than wild ancestors, and bred fruits tend to be sweeter, hardier, and often larger.

paragraphs.title: Changing Fruits (Modern Tech)
sentences: Now gene editing allows scientists to make changes to plants even more quickly and precisely.
CRISPR is the most popular such technique at the moment.
It is a technology that allows scientists to change the DNA of an organism.
It can change or remove specific genes.
That would be hard to do through selective breeding.
Computer software like artificial intelligence (AI) is also helping scientists design fruit.
With AI, computers and machines can learn and solve problems using information.
Using AI, scientists are able to discover more about certain traits, such as the chemicals that generate flavor.

socratic.q: Why might CRISPR be more efficient than traditional selective breeding?
socratic.a: Because it can change or remove specific genes quickly and precisely, while selective breeding would make such changes much harder and slower.

socratic.q: According to the paragraph, how does AI help in fruit development?
socratic.a: AI helps scientists design fruit and discover more about traits like the chemicals that generate flavor.

socratic.q: What two modern technologies does this section compare to older breeding methods?
socratic.a: Gene editing (especially CRISPR) and artificial intelligence (AI).

paragraphs.title: Slowing Reactions
sentences: Chemical reactions are when substances change into new substances.
Scientists are looking to slow chemical reactions in other fruits and veggies to make them look more appealing and even last longer.
For example, avocados (yes, they are a fruit!) turn brown when you cut into them.
That's because an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase reacts with the oxygen in the air in a process that causes browning.
Enzymes can speed up chemical reactions and are also responsible for the ripening process, which means enzymes can change the texture, color, and flavor of food, too.
GreenVenus, a Californian firm, is using CRISPR to develop avocados that don't turn brown.
They changed how the enzyme is made in the fruit.
Scientists have also developed mushrooms and potatoes that inhibit the same enzyme.
So, slowing that reaction down makes mushrooms and potatoes last longer, and they don't turn brown as fast.

socratic.q: Why do avocados turn brown after being cut?
socratic.a: An enzyme called polyphenol oxidase reacts with oxygen in the air, causing a browning process.

socratic.q: How can slowing enzyme reactions benefit fruits and vegetables?
socratic.a: It can make them look more appealing, prevent browning, and help them last longer on shelves.

socratic.q: Besides browning, what else can enzymes affect in food?
socratic.a: Enzymes are responsible for ripening and can change the texture, color, and flavor of food.

paragraphs.title: Ready To Eat?
sentences: So far, a few fruits that have been gene-edited with CRISPR have gone on sale.
That's because it takes a long time to grow most fruit.
It can take several years for apple or peach trees to begin bearing fruit.
But as more fruity creations go on sale, companies believe that more people will eat fruit.
Pairwise estimates that their seedless blackberries could become as popular as easy-peel mandarins.

socratic.q: Why have only a few gene-edited fruits reached stores so far?
socratic.a: Because most fruit takes a long time to grow; trees like apple or peach may need several years before bearing fruit.

socratic.q: What do companies believe will happen as more gene-edited fruits go on sale?
socratic.a: They believe more people will eat fruit.

socratic.q: What comparison does Pairwise make about the future of seedless blackberries?
socratic.a: They estimate seedless blackberries could become as popular as easy-peel mandarins.
